title: A reply a layer answered still carries §6.3's control flag

provenance.quote: If a NLIP end-point receives a message which has the control field set to true, it must respond with a NLIP Message with control field set to true.

reply.content: The service is in maintenance mode.

notes: `ecma-430/36` with the reply produced by a layer instead of by the handler, and the expectation is the same one for the same reason: §6.3 is unconditional and names the boolean and no other field, so the boolean goes on whichever spelling arrived and `messagetype` stays absent, because the peer never used it. The reading is `readings/51`'s — the clause is about the message the peer receives. A maintenance-mode layer is the natural way to produce this exchange: it is precisely the layer that answers every request without asking the handler, and it is precisely the one whose replies a peer reads as control replies. §6.3 is the cheapest of the three obligations to lose, because a reply that is wrong about it is still a perfectly well-formed message.
